pages.text: $(li)For Chapter 1, prioritize collecting at least 3 void steel cubes from a Greater Portal Tower to craft self-repairing diamond armor.
$(li)Tinkers’ Construct armor is viable early—build with emerald core, steel plates (Indomitable), and lead trim (Shielding); use 5 unbreakable plates for indestructibility.

$(li)Protection V on every piece is the most that does anything, and it multiplies with armor points (e.g., 50% from enchants and 50% from armor means you take 25%).$(li)Avoid Last Stand modifier; it’s unreliable and conflicts with other survivability strategies.

$(li)Jetpack is strongly recommended in blocked-flight dimensions; it cuts travel time significantly.$(li)Jetplate is useful but not mandatory.$(li)Armor Station crafts armor but cannot modify it; Armor Forge modifies but cannot craft.
$(li)Prioritize Grave Dust drop chance perk first to bulk-craft scrolls and gain Corail XP quickly.$(li)Reset with Ankh of Pray once points are high, then max Disenchanting Tome.

$(li)Scroll of Purification grants 10+ minutes of immunity to all debuffs—including Soul Fray—allowing sustainable self-sacrifice with high max health, regen, and EMC.$(li)Soul Fray prevents spamming deaths for healing; bypass it with the scroll, not avoidance.

$(li)Energy Eater does $(o)not$() refill saturation unless hunger is below full; true saturation regen (before hunger loss) is faster and more reliable.$(li)Charm of Life 2 grants undead-style revival frames: death immunity after first hit, enabling survival at very low health with multiple stacks.
$(li)With ~full inventory of Charm of Life 2, a strong weapon, and no armor, Chaos Guardian is vulnerable—even without high survivability stats—just avoid taking multiple hits in quick succession.
